Add: WordCount, Tone, Clout, Authentic, WordsPerSentence, conjunction, verb, adjective, PositiveEmotion, anxiety, Nationality2 checking numeric predictors for nonlinearity

# function:
empirical_logit_plot <- function(predictor, g = 10) {
  x <- liwc.dat[[predictor]]
  y_all <- liwc.dat[["Post1950"]]
  
  # Quantile bins (robust to ties)
  qs <- quantile(x, probs = seq(0, 1, length = g + 1), na.rm = TRUE)
  bins <- cut(x, breaks = unique(qs), include.lowest = TRUE)
  
  # Midpoints
  mid <- tapply(x, bins, mean)
  
  # Successes and totals
  y <- tapply(y_all, bins, sum)
  n <- tapply(y_all, bins, length)
  
  # Empirical logit with adjustment
  p <- (y + 0.5) / (n + 1)
  elogit <- log(p / (1 - p))
  
  # Remove NA bins
  valid <- !(is.na(mid) | is.na(elogit))
  mid <- mid[valid]
  elogit <- elogit[valid]
  
  # Plot
  plot(mid, elogit,
       xlab = predictor,
       ylab = "Empirical logit",
       main = paste("Empirical logit vs", predictor),
       pch = 16)
  
  lines(lowess(mid, elogit), col = "blue", lwd = 2)
}

WordCount, Tone, Clout, Authentic, WordsPerSentence, conjunction, verb, adjective, PositiveEmotion, anxiety,

Initial Model Fitting

Initial model using main effects based on EDA

Add: WordCount, Tone, Clout, Authentic, WordsPerSentence, conjunction, verb, adjective, PositiveEmotion, anxiety, Nationality2

m1 = glm(Post1950~WordCount+Tone+Clout+Authentic+WordsPerSentence+conjunction+verb+adjective+Nationality2,data=liwc.dat,family=binomial)
summary(m1)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = Post1950 ~ WordCount + Tone + Clout + Authentic + 
##     WordsPerSentence + conjunction + verb + adjective + Nationality2, 
##     family = binomial, data = liwc.dat)
## 
## Coefficients:
##                       Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)          3.941e+00  3.070e+00   1.284 0.199263    
## WordCount            2.245e-06  2.056e-06   1.092 0.274824    
## Tone                -4.247e-02  1.182e-02  -3.593 0.000327 ***
## Clout                4.422e-02  2.672e-02   1.655 0.097896 .  
## Authentic            8.459e-02  1.750e-02   4.834 1.34e-06 ***
## WordsPerSentence    -2.524e-01  4.420e-02  -5.711 1.12e-08 ***
## conjunction         -5.319e-01  1.555e-01  -3.420 0.000626 ***
## verb                 9.926e-02  6.910e-02   1.437 0.150849    
## adjective           -2.835e-01  2.759e-01  -1.027 0.304248    
## Nationality2British -4.570e-01  2.395e-01  -1.908 0.056369 .  
## Nationality2Other    3.498e-02  3.134e-01   0.112 0.911137    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 876.39  on 690  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 544.51  on 680  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 566.51
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 6
# Use step() function to see what main effects it chooses
# I chose not to put very obviously correlated variables / variables that are a subset of others in the upper scope of the function
# - Didn't use Period, Comma, Colon, SemiC, QMark, Exclam, Dash, Quote, Apostrophe, Parenthesis, OtherPunctuation (subset of AllPunc)
# - Didn't use i, we, you, SheHe,they, PersonalPronouns, ImpersonalPronouns (subset of pronoun)

cor(liwc.dat$PositiveEmotion,liwc.dat$Tone) # don't use PositionEmotion or NegativeEmotion (Tone is directly based on them)
## [1] 0.7889969
cor(liwc.dat$verb,liwc.dat$AuxiliaryVerb) # don't use AuxiliaryVerb
## [1] 0.8110573
cor(liwc.dat$verb,liwc.dat$adverb) # don't use adverb
## [1] 0.6391945
cor(liwc.dat$AnalyticalThinking,liwc.dat$FunctionWords) # don't use FunctionWords
## [1] -0.6282037
mStep = step(m1,scope=list(lower=~1,upper=~Sex+WordCount+AnalyticalThinking+Clout+Authentic+Tone+WordsPerSentence+SixLetters+pronoun+article+preposition+conjunction+negation+verb+adjective+number+AllPunc+Nationality2),trace=0)
summary(mStep)
##

## glm(formula = Post1950 ~ Tone + Clout + Authentic + WordsPerSentence + 
##     conjunction + verb + Nationality2 + AllPunc + number + SixLetters, 
##     family = binomial, data = liwc.dat)

AIC(m1)
## [1] 566.5052
AIC(mStep)
## [1] 510.4605
BIC(m1)
## [1] 616.4247
BIC(mStep)
## [1] 564.9181
# So we can see that AIC (as expected) and BIC are better for the step() function model. 

# conjunction is insignificant according to Wald test in model: check with LRT and BIC metrics
mStep_adj = update(mStep, . ~ . -conjunction)
anova(mStep_adj,mStep,'LRT') # p-value > 0.05, which suggests conjunction should be removed
## Analysis of Deviance Table

Interaction terms:

# Add based on theoretical plausibility and then use step() and LRTs to see if their addition is helpful
# List of plausible interactions to add:
# - Tone*Authentic
# - Tone*Clout
# - Tone*Nationality2
# - Clout*Authentic

mInteractions = update(mStep_adj, . ~ . +(Tone*Authentic) +(Tone*Clout) +(Tone*Nationality2) +(Clout*Authentic))
summary(mInteractions)

# Next I will use the step() function with lower scope as mStep_adj and upper scope as mInteractions. This will hopefully land on a model that optimizes AIC while remaining consistent with our EDA and theoretical plausibility.
mStep_int = step(mInteractions,scope=list(lower=mStep_adj,upper=mInteractions))

# p-value > 0.05. This supports that the additional interaction term included mInteractions (that aren't in mStep_int) are NOT worth including
anova(mStep_adj,mStep_int,"LRT")
## Analysis of Deviance Table

## Model 1: Post1950 ~ Tone + Clout + Authentic + WordsPerSentence + verb + 
##     Nationality2 + AllPunc + number + SixLetters

# p-value < 0.05. This supports that the interaction terms included in mStep_int (which aren't in mStep_adj) are worth adding.

# 3 out of 4 of the predictors that showed curvature in the empirical logit plots have been removed. I will try adding all of their quadratic effects regardless
mQuadratic = update(mStep_int, . ~ . + I(WordCount^2) + I(Clout^2) + I(adjective^2) + I(conjunction^2))
summary(mQuadratic)
##

Inference

(exp_coef = exp(coef(fm)))
##              (Intercept)                     Tone                    Clout 
##             3.156872e+07             4.946172e-01             8.450284e-01 
##                Authentic         WordsPerSentence                     verb

##               SixLetters           Tone:Authentic               Tone:Clout

## Tone:Nationality2British   Tone:Nationality2Other 
##             1.052224e+00             9.227443e-01
# WordsPerSentence (0.631): Holding other variables constant, an increase in average word per sentence by 1 word decreases the odds of a novel being post-1950 by about 36.9%.
# verb (1.363): Holding other variables constant, a 1% increase in verb usage increases the odds of a novel being post-1950 by about 36.3%. 
# AllPunc (0.823): Holding other variables constant, a 1% increase in punctuation usage decreases the odds of a novel being post-1950 by about 17.7%
# SixLetters (1.481): Holding other variables constant, a 1% increase in words longer than 6 letters increases the odds of a novel being post-1950 by about 48.1%

The effects of Tone, Authentic, Clout and Nationality2 cannot be interpreted independently due to their inclusion in interaction term(s).

# Tone*Authentic (1.005): As Authentic increases, the negative effect of Tone becomes slightly weaker
# Tone*Clout (1.007): As Clout increases, the negative effect of Tone becomes slightly weaker
# Tone*Nationality2British (1.052): For British novels, the negative effect of Tone is slightly weaker than for American novels
# Tone*Nationality2Other (0.923): For "Other" nationality novels, the negative effect of Tone is slightly stronger than for American novels.

# WordsPerSentence (0.57 to 0.69): Each 1-word increase per sentence decreases the odds of being post-1950 by about 31-43% (stable negative)
# verb (1.16 to 1.61): Each 1% increase in verb usage increases the odds of being post-1950 by 16-61%. (stable positive)
# AllPunc (0.77 to 0.88): Each 1% increase in punctuation decreases odds by 12-23%. (stable negative)
# SixLetters (1.29 to 1.72): Each 1% increase in words longer than 6 letters increases odds of being post-1950 by 29-72%. (stable positive)

# Tone (0.30 to 0.81): Holding other variables at reference levels for interactions, a 1-unit increase in Tone score is associated with a 19-70% decrease in the odds of a novel being post-1950. 
# Both Clout and Authentic main effects include 1, so the main effect cannot be considered significant

# Tone*Authentic (1.002 to 1.009): As Authenticity increases, the effect of Tone on the odds of post-1950 becomes slightly less negative
# Tone*Clout (1.002 to 1.013): As Clout increases, the effect of Tone becomes slightly less negative
# Both Tone*Nationality2 ineractions include 1, so the interaction effect is unclear.

Diagnostics

Checking model fit

# Quantile residuals vs linear predictor
library(statmod)
## Warning: package 'statmod' was built under R version 4.5.2
rQ = qresid(fm) # quantile residuals (authors of GLMR advocate)
rQ.std = rQ/sqrt(1-hatvalues(fm))
scatter.smooth(rQ.std~fm$linear.predictors, las=1,ylab="Standardized quantile residual",xlab = "Linear predictors",col="grey")

# No clear patterns, indicating that the model is a good fit. 

library(pROC)

Misspecifications

eta = fm$linear.predictors
mu = fitted(fm)
y = liwc.dat$Post1950

z <- eta + (y - mu) / (mu * (1 - mu))
# truncate extreme values for plotting
z_trunc <- pmin(pmax(z, -10), 10)

plot(eta, z_trunc, pch = 16,
     xlab = "Linear Predictor", ylab = "Working Response (z)")
lines(lowess(eta, z_trunc), col='blue',lwd = 2)

# A bit of curvature in the center; link function issue?

# Although none of the plots are too alarming regarding nonlinearity, there are clearly some potential outliers. Therefore, I will deviate a bit from my plan and also use DFFITS to identify influential points and refit a model without them included. Then I will look for differences in the coefficients of the model with and the model without these points.  

im.fm = influence.measures(fm)

n = nrow(fm$model)
p = length(coef(fm))
dffits_vals = im.fm$infmat[,'dffit']
cutoff = 2*sqrt(p/n)
id.inf = which(abs(dffits_vals) > cutoff)
fm.omit = update(fm, subset = -id.inf)

exp(coef(fm))

GLMM

author_counts = table(liwc.dat$AuthorID)
length(unique(liwc.dat$AuthorID))
## [1] 301
hist(author_counts,breaks=50)

# Quite a few authors have multiple novels in the data set

author_1950=aggregate(Post1950 ~ AuthorID, data = liwc.dat, FUN = mean)
hist(author_1950$Post1950, breaks = 10,main = "Author's Novels Post1950",xlab = "Proportion Post1950")

# This is important because it means most of the authors contribute either exclusively pre-1950 or exclusively post-1950 novels. This will introduce confounding, breaking the usual purpose of random effect. Because of this, there is very little within-author variation in the response
# Differences in predictors might just reflect which authors are in each era, not true linguistic change over time

# So, my goal with fitting this GLMM is now: if I account for which author texts come from, do the relationships identified from GLM still hold.

library(lme4)
## Loading required package: Matrix
m_glmm=glmer(Post1950~ Tone+Clout+Authentic+WordsPerSentence+verb+AllPunc+SixLetters+Nationality2+Tone:Authentic+Tone:Clout+Tone:Nationality2+ (1|AuthorID),family = binomial,data = liwc.dat)
## Warning in checkConv(attr(opt, "derivs"), opt$par, ctrl = control$checkConv, :
## Model failed to converge with max|grad| = 83.1828 (tol = 0.002, component 1)
## Warning in checkConv(attr(opt, "derivs"), opt$par, ctrl = control$checkConv, : Model is nearly unidentifiable: very large eigenvalue
##  - Rescale variables?;Model is nearly unidentifiable: large eigenvalue ratio
##  - Rescale variables?
# large eigenvalue ratio: rescale variables 
liwc.dat$Tone <- scale(liwc.dat$Tone)
liwc.dat$Clout <- scale(liwc.dat$Clout)
liwc.dat$Authentic <- scale(liwc.dat$Authentic)
liwc.dat$WordsPerSentence <- scale(liwc.dat$WordsPerSentence)
liwc.dat$verb <- scale(liwc.dat$verb)
liwc.dat$AllPunc <- scale(liwc.dat$AllPunc)
liwc.dat$SixLetters <- scale(liwc.dat$SixLetters)

m_glmm=glmer(Post1950~Tone+Clout+Authentic+WordsPerSentence+verb+AllPunc+SixLetters+Nationality2+ Tone:Authentic+Tone:Clout+Tone:Nationality2+(1|AuthorID),family = binomial,data = liwc.dat)
## Warning in checkConv(attr(opt, "derivs"), opt$par, ctrl = control$checkConv, :
## Model failed to converge with max|grad| = 2.48894 (tol = 0.002, component 1)
# failed to converge with max|grad| = 2.39944
# switch optimizer
m_glmm=glmer(Post1950 ~ Tone + Clout + Authentic + WordsPerSentence +verb + AllPunc + SixLetters + Nationality2 + Tone:Authentic+Tone:Clout+Tone:Nationality2 + (1 | AuthorID),family = binomial,data = liwc.dat,control = glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
summary(m_glmm)

# Which effects are still significant:
# Tone, WordsPerSentence, AllPunc, SixLetters and Verb are still significant. 
# So, Tone, WordsPerSentence, AllPunc and SixLetters remain predictive of era even after accounting for the strong author-level confounding. This suggests that these linguistic differences are robust across time periods (rather than just being driven by differences between authors.
# However, interaction effects between Tone and Authentic and between Tone and Clout, which were significant in the GLM, did not remain significant. This suggests these interaction effects are likely driven by differences in which authors appear in each time period.
